CodeReviewCategoryCounts.description:
Unresolved findings per cited-Learning category in the review summary.

A finding joins a category by citing a Learning of that category, so only
Learning-citing findings count here (mirrors the "Learnings cited" row, not
"Findings"). Counts are UNRESOLVED only, matching `severity_counts` —
a fixed finding is not work left to do.
CodeReviewCategoryCounts.title: CodeReviewCategoryCounts

CodeReviewDetailFinding.description:
A finding plus the source it replaces, for the detail page's diff.

Extends rather than widening `CodeReviewFindingPublic`: that schema also
serves pipeline findings, which are not anchored to an `old_string` and so
can never carry a snapshot. Adding the fields there would hand every
consumer three columns that are permanently null on half the rows.

All three are absent together or present together — a finding anchored by
`posting_range` has no snapshot row, and the card falls back to rendering the
replacement alone.

acknowledged.description:
The developer accepted this finding and kept the code as it is.

Distinct from `withdrawn`: the finding was correct. A client that showed
both as one "closed without a fix" state would be telling the reader the
review made a mistake it did not make.
acknowledged.title: Acknowledged

withdrawn.description:
The agent accepted a rebuttal and retracted this finding.

Derived here so no client re-derives it from a timestamp.
withdrawn.title: Withdrawn

CodeReviewDetailFinding.title: CodeReviewDetailFinding

CodeReviewMergeRequestDetail.description: Single merge-request review detail (header + stats + findings).
CodeReviewMergeRequestDetail.title: CodeReviewMergeRequestDetail

CodeReviewSeverityCounts.description:
Unresolved finding counts per severity, for the review-summary panel.

Severity is chosen over specialist deliberately: FAST reviews write
`specialist='main_agent'` for every finding, so a specialist breakdown reads
100% "other" on them. Severity is set on every finding in every review mode.

Counts are UNRESOLVED only, matching `unresolved_findings_count` and the
verdict rules — a fixed finding is not work left to do.
CodeReviewSeverityCounts.title: CodeReviewSeverityCounts

RefreshTokenRequest.description:
Request to refresh access token.

Attributes:
    refresh_token: The refresh token JWT. Optional — the cookie-auth flow
        sends it as an httpOnly cookie and omits the body field.
    workspace_id: Optional workspace context to include in new access token.
        The organization_id is derived from the workspace's organization.
RefreshTokenRequest.title: RefreshTokenRequest

ReviewEffort.description:
How much reviewer attention a change likely demands, as a triage badge.

A single glance signal next to the verdict: LIGHT changes can be skimmed,
HEAVY ones deserve a careful pass. Derived from diff size (files + lines) in
`domain/review_effort.py`, NOT the AI quality `score` — a small change can be
low-quality and a huge one clean, so effort and score are orthogonal axes.

Absent (NULL on the detail) when no diff-stats were ever recorded, so the
badge stays hidden rather than mislabelling an unmeasured MR as LIGHT.
ReviewEffort.title: ReviewEffort

SnapshotFileChangeType.description:
Whether the file the finding sits in was added or modified by the MR.

Drives how the detail page tints the finding's lines: a newly-added file
reads as green (its lines are additions, matching the provider's own diff),
a modified file reads as a red "current" line the fix replaces. Stored as its
string value in a VARCHAR column, never a native Postgres enum, so
UPPER()/LOWER() and enum-type migrations (DB-02) never enter the picture.

Absent (NULL) when the file's status could not be determined at review time,
or for a `posting_range` finding that has no snapshot row at all.
SnapshotFileChangeType.title: SnapshotFileChangeType

SubmitHeadlessRunRequest.description:
Body for `POST /cli/runs`.

`agent_mode` is intentionally NOT exposed in V1 — the server picks the tier
(Starter is coerced to Light at submit; every other plan runs the default).

conversation_id.description: Optional. Continue this existing conversation (a run is attached to it) instead of creating a new one. Must belong to the authenticated workspace and be a chat-type conversation (HEADLESS or CHAT).
conversation_id.title: Conversation Id

idempotency_key.description: Optional caller-supplied key (workspace-scoped). A retried submit with the same key returns the original run instead of creating a duplicate. Omit for at-least-once submit.
idempotency_key.title: SubmitHeadlessRunRequest_idempotency_key

source_conversation_id.description: Optional. The AGENT_CLI conversation whose terminal watches this run. Only for a new run: it cannot be combined with `conversation_id`. Must belong to the authenticated workspace.
source_conversation_id.title: Source Conversation Id

SubmitHeadlessRunRequest.title: SubmitHeadlessRunRequest

TicketComplianceStatus.description:
How well the MR satisfies its linked ticket's acceptance criteria.

Only meaningful when the review found a linked Jira/Linear ticket and read
its acceptance criteria (the reviewer already fetches these via the
reviewing-jira / reviewing-linear skill). Absent (NULL) when no ticket was
linked — the detail's compliance card then hides rather than claiming
coverage it never assessed.

Stored as its string value in a VARCHAR column, never a native Postgres
enum, so UPPER()/LOWER() and enum-type migrations (DB-02) never enter the
picture — same treatment as the sibling SnapshotFileChangeType. Lives here
(data/models) rather than in api/schemas so the column can be typed with it
and the write path stops passing bare strings; api/schemas re-exports it for
the response model. The agent-facing tool declares the same value set as an
inline Literal (the repo prefers inline Literals in model-visible schemas
over $ref/$defs); a parity test pins the two equal.
TicketComplianceStatus.title: TicketComplianceStatus

WorkspaceRole.description:
Workspace-level roles for RBAC.

Role hierarchy (highest to lowest):
- ADMIN: Full control within workspace
- DEVELOPER: Can use chat, view resources, manage recommendations
- VIEWER: Read-only access

Note: OWNER is deprecated. Use organization-level roles instead:
- ORG_OWNER/ORG_ADMIN inherit to ADMIN in all workspaces
- ORG_DEVELOPER inherits to DEVELOPER in all workspaces
- ORG_VIEWER inherits to VIEWER in all workspaces
WorkspaceRole.title: WorkspaceRole

post.description: Create a short-lived device authorization for an outbound-only CLI.
Poll until approved, denied, expired, or asked to slow down.

Exchange a one-time code + PKCE verifier for a Token.

Any failure (missing / expired code, verifier mismatch) returns the same
generic 400 so a stolen code cannot be probed for its state (CA-SP-3).

Logout user by revoking refresh token.

This is a best-effort operation that always succeeds. The refresh token is
read from the httpOnly cookie first, falling back to the body for legacy
clients. Auth cookies are always cleared. If the refresh token is invalid
or already revoked, we still return success.

Refresh access token with mandatory rotation.
Following Auth0 best practices.

The refresh token is read from the httpOnly cookie first, falling back to
the request body for legacy header-based clients during the migration. The
organization_id is derived from the workspace_id. If no workspace is
provided, falls back to the user's oldest active organization membership.

get.description:
Get workspaces - both owned and invited (non-deleted only).
Filtered by current organization context from token.
Supports search by workspace name.

post.description:
Create new workspace. Requires WORKSPACE_CREATE permission.

Workspace is created in the current organization context from token.
